title: Command-line options override single fields of Scan.toml
description: all-fields has 1 HIGH (ballerina:13), 2 MEDIUM and 3 LOW issues, and a Scan.toml that writes [rule] exclude, [suppression] enabled and requireReason, [gate] failOnSeverity and failOnCount, and [analysis] excludeTests. Each option replaces only its own field and warns only when the file writes that field with a different value. A rule option that leaves both include and exclude set is a usage error.

steps.name: Scan.toml alone
steps.note: ballerina:13 is excluded; 2 issues at or above MEDIUM reach failOnCount = 2: exit 1.

steps.name: --fail-on-count=5
steps.note: One warning for failOnCount; failOnSeverity = "MEDIUM" is kept, 2 < 5, passes.

steps.name: --fail-on-count=2 (same value)
steps.note: No warning; fails as with Scan.toml alone.

steps.name: --fail-on-severity=HIGH --fail-on-count=1
steps.note: Two warnings, one per field. The HIGH issue is excluded by Scan.toml, so it passes.

steps.name: --exclude-rules=ballerina:1
steps.note: Replaces [rule] exclude, with a warning; ballerina:13 is back, 3 issues at or above MEDIUM, fails.

steps.name: --include-rules=ballerina:1 (conflict)
steps.note: include from the command line and exclude from Scan.toml are both set: usage error, exit 2, before scanning.

steps.name: Suppression flags
steps.note: Warnings for enabled and requireReason; none for requireRuleId, which the file does not write.
